title: Dark Horse DH-155-12
subtitle: High-Speed Sweater / Knitwear Fast Linking Machine

purposeAndApplication.purpose: The DH-155-12 is a sweater and knitwear fast linking machine. Its main purpose is to join knitted garment parts such as front panels, back panels, sleeves, collars, cuffs, and side seams by connecting the loops or edges of two knitted panels. The machine works by guiding knitted panels through a linking zone where the needle and looper form a flexible joining seam suitable for knitwear.
applications: Linking sweater front body and back body panels together
Joining sleeves to the sweater body at the shoulder and armhole seam
Attaching knitted collars, cuffs, and rib waistbands to garment panels
Joining side seam panels on sweaters, cardigans, and knit pullovers
Any loop-to-loop or edge-to-edge joining of 12GG knitted garment parts
purposeAndApplication.industry: Sweater and knitwear manufacturing, knitted garment assembly, cardigan and pullover production, any factory producing knitted garments requiring panel linking

overviewDescription: The Dark Horse DH-155-12 is a sweater and knitwear fast linking machine manufactured by WULIN JIXIE CO. LTD (China). 'Dark Horse' is the brand/trade name, 'DH' stands for Dark Horse, '155' is the model number, and '12' indicates 12 gauge (12GG) specification. The machine joins knitted garment panels by connecting loops or edges using a needle and looper mechanism that forms a flexible chain-style linking seam. The gauge specification must be confirmed from the actual machine nameplate, installed needle/dial parts, and supplier documentation.

workingPrinciples.heading: 1. Basic Linking Principle
workingPrinciples.description: Two knitted parts are placed together at the required seam position. The operator aligns the edge loops or seam allowance. The machine feeds the joined edge through the linking zone. The needle enters the knitted edge, the looper catches the thread and forms a loop, and the next needle movement locks the previous loop with the new loop. A continuous flexible linking seam is formed.

workingPrinciples.heading: 2. Why Linking Differs from Normal Sewing
workingPrinciples.description: A linking machine joins knitted garment panels by connecting loops or edges, producing a flexible seam suitable for knitwear that stretches. A plain sewing machine forms a lockstitch seam that may not match the knit-loop structure. Linking requires high operator alignment skill and produces a clean linked seam with chain-stitch style structure on the back.

workingPrinciples.heading: 3. Needle and Looper Timing
workingPrinciples.description: The most critical adjustment is the timing between the needle and the looper. The looper must catch the thread loop at the correct moment. Incorrect timing causes skipped stitches, loose seams, thread breakage, or needle damage. Correct timing produces smooth linking, stable stitch formation, and a clean seam.

workingPrinciples.heading: 4. Gauge Matching
workingPrinciples.description: In knitwear, gauge means the number of needles or loops per inch. A 12GG fabric has a finer loop structure than lower-gauge fabrics. The linking machine must match the garment's gauge. If the linking gauge does not match the sweater gauge, the seam may become uneven, loose, tight, wavy, or visually defective. Confirm gauge from machine nameplate, needle/dial specification, and sample seam quality.

workingPrinciples.heading: 5. Thread Tension and Feed
workingPrinciples.description: Thread tension must remain balanced throughout the linking operation. Too much tension causes seam tightness or breakage; too little tension causes a loose seam and poor appearance. The feed mechanism moves the knitted parts forward at a controlled rate. The operator must guide panels smoothly without pulling, as knitted fabric stretches easily.

finalNotes:
• Commercial Identity: Brand/trade name is 'Dark Horse'. DH = Dark Horse, 155 = model number, 12 = 12 gauge/12GG. Manufacturing company is WULIN JIXIE CO. LTD (China).
• Gauge Verification: The suffix '12' indicates 12GG. Always confirm from machine nameplate, installed needle/dial parts, and supplier documentation before production.
• Spare Parts: Do not rely only on the model name for ordering. Always confirm by physical part comparison, supplier part number, machine nameplate, and actual installed assembly — DH-155 machines may have different market versions and gauge configurations.
• Needle-Looper Timing: The most critical adjustment. Check timing when skipped stitches occur repeatedly even after needle replacement.
• Fabric Handling: Never pull sweater panels during linking — knitted fabric stretches easily and pulling will distort measurements and seam quality.
• Thread Path: Keep thread path clean and free from lint. Any burr on guides can cut thread repeatedly.
• Quality Check Points: Check gauge matching, needle condition, threading, tension balance, fabric guiding, thread path cleanliness, needle-looper timing, and feed parts regularly.
